name: Pyramid noise (multi-resolution, sonar)
plain: Adds lower-resolution Gaussian noise layers on top of white noise with decaying weights, to give more low-frequency energy. Random downscale factor at each iteration. The most common approach to multi-res noise.
math:
n = ε. For i in 0..iterations(10): r~U(2,4); w←max(1,int(w/r^i)), h likewise (note the divisor compounds); n ← n + up(N(0,I)@h×w)·discount^i (discount=.7); break at 1.
Then normalized to unit std by scale_noise.
Highres: same with upscaling grids up to 15×, base uniform-based, then downsampled. r^i and U(2,4).
Mix variants: pyramid_mix: 0.2·P₁ − 0.8·P₂ (discount .6). pyramid_discount5: discount=.5.

props.normalizes_variance: yes in sonar and ULS and BFS; varies elsewhere

label: from code
surprise: Sonar's added layers call torch.randn without the seeded generator (noise_generation.py:632), so they follow the global RNG.

audit.note: "Highres: same" hides different defaults: iterations 4 (not 10), a uniform base, and grids growing up to 15×, compounding h,w (blepping__ComfyUI-sonar/py/noise_generation.py:527-561). Layers after the base draw randn without the seeded generator (lines 630-640), so they are not governed by the generator. "Most common approach" is opinion, not checkable from code.
